code: struct ofpbuf properties = ofpbuf_const_initializer(ofpbuf_pull(msg, len), len);
note: Attacker-controlled property bytes from the raw OpenFlow 1.4 port-stats reply are exposed for parsing; the properties buffer is bounded only by the message length.
The Intel experimenter property payload header (type/length/experimenter/exp_type/pad/stats_array_size) is interpreted directly from the attacker-controlled message.
Attacker-controlled stats_array_size (set to 1 in the PoC) drives the number of parse-loop iterations.
Attacker-controlled length field (set to 16, the header-only size) is taken as the bounds reference for the parse loop.
The cursor is advanced past previously parsed entries; with no entries present, 'current' lands exactly at payload offset 16, i.e. one byte past the 16-byte property payload.

Bounds check is performed only AFTER the size byte has already been dereferenced and it compares against the attacker-controlled msg_size instead of the real payload size, so it can never stop the out-of-bounds read.
Out-of-bounds read: '*current' dereferences one byte past the end of the 16-byte property payload (message byte 112 of the 112-byte input), a heap-buffer-overread detected under ASAN.
